subject: Rate card & packaging questions — vector embeddings (dimensions / discounts / export)
messages:
From: Alan Cho <alan.cho@oliveanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Rate card request — embeddings / vector pricing and packaging

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking a look at our RFP. We're evaluating a vendor for our vector search layer and want to understand Redwood's hosted embeddings economics before we build anything heavier. A few specific asks to help our procurement and ML infra teams: 

- Baseline hosted API pricing for embeddings (prefer both per-vector and per-token equivalents if you show that way).
- Pricing by vector dimensionality (we're looking at 768, 1536, and 2048) — do you price per-dimension or per-vector?
- Supported models and how model choice affects price/throughput (we're exploring both smaller cheaper models and higher-dim higher-accuracy models).
- Volume tiers/discounts for sustained commits (our forecast: 100M vectors/month in steady state, with spikey onboarding months).
- Any packaging options for committed vs on-demand (monthly commit, Dedicated capacity, Private deployment notes).
- Export/ownership: are produced embeddings exportable for in-house vector stores? Any constraints on retention or export formats?

Attached is the RFP and a short usage profile (Q4 ingest schedule). Can you summarize an apples-to-apples baseline and call out where cost tradeoffs typically show up (storage, write API, read API, batch vs realtime)?

Cheers,
Alan
Alan Cho
Head of ML Ops | Olive Analytics
procurement@oliveanalytics.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Rate card request — embeddings / vector pricing and packaging

Hi Alan —

Thanks for the clear RFP and the usage breakdown. High level answers first, then I'll attach a short rate-card and a model-comparison CSV. Marissa (cc'ed) will help with the committed-plan examples.

Baseline hosted API (short):
- Pricing unit: we bill per-vector (each API embed call returns one vector per input item). Dimension affects model selection and therefore the unit price — we do not multiply price by dimension count; instead we publish model-specific per-vector rates.
- Example list prices (hosted, pay-as-you-go):
  - redwood-embed-lite (768d): $0.00018 per vector
  - redwood-embed-standard (1536d): $0.00036 per vector
  - redwood-embed-pro (2048d): $0.00054 per vector

Volume discounts / packaging:
- Standard tiering (applies to hosted usage): 10M+ vectors/month = 12% off list; 50M+ = 25% off; 100M+ = custom enterprise pricing (usually 35–50% depending on commit and term).
- Committed monthly plans: we can convert a committed vector volume into a lower effective per-vector price and add burst protection. Dedicated pools are recommended for steady high-throughput production to guarantee latency SLOs — separate contract/seat pricing applies.

Model / throughput notes:
- Model choice affects both accuracy and serving latency. For example, redwood-embed-pro (2048d) typically increases storage and index costs ~1.3–1.5x vs 1536d and has higher GPU inference costs; it's ideal for high-recall semantic search. redwood-embed-lite is fast and cheap for recall-sensitive applications with tight cost constraints.
- Supported hosted models: redwood-embed-lite, redwood-embed-standard, redwood-embed-pro, and curated open models (text-embedding-3-small, text-embedding-3-large). We can run a small A/B eval on your sample dataset to recommend the best fit.

Export & retention:
- Embeddings you generate via the hosted API are exportable in JSON/CSV/npz. Customers retain ownership. For Private deployments we can disable host-side retention per contract; hosted accounts have configurable retention windows.

Attachments: I'm including a condensed ratecard spreadsheet and a model-dimension compare CSV (attached). I'll also add an apples-to-apples example TCO for Hosted vs Dedicated in the follow-up.

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to walk through the numbers?

Best,

Soojin —

Thanks for the quick summary and the spreadsheet. A couple of clarifying items before we set a call: 

1) You said "per-vector" pricing and model-specific rates. Can you confirm that a single API response containing a 1536-d vector is billed the same whether we request one vector or batch 100 vectors in the same call (i.e., billing is per vector produced, not per request)? Also, does padding or returning optional metadata affect the unit billing?

2) For storage impact, do you charge separately for hosted storage of embeddings (long-term storage for similarity search) or is that outside the hosted embeddings unit price? If separate, what are typical monthly $/GB figures for the vectors once indexed?

3) Can you provide a sample TCO (hosted vs Dedicated) for our forecast (100M vectors/month) with a 12-month term? We're trying to compare the effective per-vector cost after commit and estimated index/storage costs.

4) Any constraints on exporting embeddings if we choose to stop using Redwood hosted? We need clean export for in-house FAISS reindexing.

If you can send short bullets on 1–4 we can decide whether to proceed to a budgetary PO or ask procurement to run a commercial terms call.

—Alan

Alan —

Short answers to your 4 bullets, then an example calculation attached: 

1) Billing unit: per-vector (yes) — whether you send 1 vector in 100 separate calls or 100 vectors in one batched call, billing counts the vectors produced. Returning optional metadata (trace ids, request tags) does not change vector billing. If you request multiple models in a single call (e.g., light + pro for comparisons) each produced vector is billed at that model's unit price.

2) Storage: hosted embeddings retention and indexing are billed separately. Typical range for persisted vector storage and index maintenance is $0.03–$0.09 per GB/month depending on index type (flat vs HNSW/IVF) and replication. In our example sheet I included approximate storage multipliers by dim: 768d ~ 0.6x, 1536d ~ 1x, 2048d ~ 1.33x relative to the 1536 baseline.

3) TCO sample (100M vectors/mo, hosted, 12-month):
- List math (hosted pay-as-you-go, 1536d at $0.00036): base = $36,000/month (100M * $0.00036)
- Apply typical enterprise committed discount (35% for a 100M/mo 12-month commit): effective = $23,400/month
- Storage & indexing estimate: assume 1536d at 1.0x => ~2.5 TB raw vectors (compressed/indexed factors reduce this) => estimated $0.05/GB => ~$125/month storage (example index + replicas increases this; see spreadsheet).
- Dedicated/Private: for sustained 100M vectors/mo we often recommend Dedicated capacity because it lowers per-vector inference spend and gives consistent latency — final Dedicated pricing depends on pool size and reserved GPU months, but ballpark total cost typically reduces inference spend by 20–40% vs hosted list when amortized over a commit. We included a Worked Example tab in the spreadsheet.

4) Export: yes — customers can export embeddings in common formats. We include tooling to bulk export via signed S3 or direct download. For Private deployments customers control the data. We do require a short deprovisioning window for hosted accounts (typically 14 days) to allow for graceful export.

Next steps: 
- If you want, Marissa and I will prepare a draft commercial term sheet with a 12-month 100M commit and the custom discount band (and include Dedicated vs Hosted total cost comparisons).
- Proposed 30-min review: Thu 26 Nov 10:00am PT — confirm and we'll send a calendar invite.
